item.title: ‘It’s called bodybuilding, not plastic building’: Champ alleges fake muscles
item.description: Four-time women's bodybuilding champion Sarah Villegas recently granted an exclusive interview to USA TODAY Sports about a massive controversy that's shaken up her sport. She has accused rival Natalia Coelho of getting injected with a Plexiglas substance to build fake "plastic" muscles before winning the Ms. Olympia event for best women’s physique in 2025. She made this claim after obtaining unsolicited "firsthand" information about it from a licensed health professional at the clinic in Brazil where the procedure allegedly took place. USA TODAY reviewed this information and confirmed with this person that they shared it with Villegas. The person didn't want to be identified for fear of retaliation. Injecting Plexiglass? A champion cried foul. Bodybuilding’s response raises more questions Coelho hasn’t denied or confirmed the allegation and didn't return messages seeking comment. Coelho again won the crown for best physique at Ms. Olympia in September, beating Villegas for the second year in a row. The Olympia event is the "Super Bowl" of pro bodybuilding. Here is the interview with Villegas. What caused you to suspect this with Natalia Coelho? Villegas: I first became suspicious and spoke up publicly on this when I noticed what I thought was an abrupt change in Natalia Coelho's legs at the 2025 Pittsburgh Pro, just a few months before the 2025 Olympia. I was still the reigning and defending Olympia Champion at the time. I had noticed that her legs changed their natural genetic shape, and displayed what I thought was a humanly impossible change in volume in a very short period of time. Why did you go public initially? (Villegas posted a message on Instagram about her suspicions last year and followed up with more after that . Some described her as a "sore loser" in response.) Villegas: I went public to bring attention to what I think is an existential issue. Existential to the future of the sport of bodybuilding and to the future of my own career. In my opinion, the sport of bodybuilding will not survive for long if a world champion can stand on stage displaying muscles that aren't actually muscle. Did you suspect it was PMMA (Plexiglas) before getting information about it from the clinic worker? (PMMA is polymethyl methacrylate, also known commercially as Plexiglas. The Boston Bruins have completed 18 games of the 2026-27 NHL season, and their early success is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook. Boston improved to 13-4-1 with Sunday's 4-1 victory over the Florida Panthers, extending its winning streak to four games. The Bruins have collected 27 of a possible 36 standings points, putting them atop the Atlantic Division and among the NHL's strongest teams. The record is impressive, but several underlying numbers provide an even better explanation of what has made Boston so successful. Boston's Goal Differential Tells A Powerful Story Through 18 games, the Bruins have scored 67 goals while allowing only 41, producing an impressive plus-26 goal differential. That works out to approximately 3.72 goals scored and 2.28 goals allowed per game, a combination that gives Boston a considerable advantage on most nights. The Bruins then experienced another difficult stretch with consecutive losses to Carolina and St. Louis, but their response has been encouraging. They have won four straight games since October 31, defeating Chicago, Vegas, Pittsburgh and Florida. item.title: It will happen eventually: El Mala drops a transfer hint
item.description: It will happen eventually: El Mala drops a transfer hint Despite receiving numerous offers last summer, 20-year-old Said El Mala decided to stay at 1. FC Köln and sign a long-term contract extension until 2031. Now the Germany international has explained the reasons behind his decision. Speaking to RTL and Sky, the forward reflected on the transfer window: “I chose Köln because I simply felt at home here. I didn’t want to leave, even though there were a lot of inquiries.” He made no secret in the interview of having considered offers from other clubs: “Of course, we listened to everything. That’s completely normal.” Ultimately, however, the club’s sporting prospects tipped the balance in favor of staying. Speaking to the two TV broadcasters, El Mala explained: “But I spoke a lot with the board and the coach and listened to their plans for the team. Looking at things now, those plans have been put into practice exactly as discussed. I want to make the city and the club happy through my performances and those of the team.” There was certainly no shortage of high-profile suitors in the summer. Among them, English Premier League club Brighton & Hove Albion sounded out a move for the youngster. Borussia Dortmund were also reportedly prepared to put a transfer fee of around €50 million on the table, but Köln’s management felt that was too little. Given his potential, keeping the forward at Köln for the long term is considered unlikely. Asked about his future career ambitions by RTL and Sky, the 20-year-old made an eye-catching statement: “There are always dreams. I want to achieve a lot one day and play in the Champions League too. I can’t say when that moment will come. But it will happen someday.” This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: A C.J. Stroud flu game? Sick and with the chills, Texans QB throws for 5 TDs to beat Chargers
item.description: Back in his native Southern California, C.J. Stroud turned in one of the best games of his career as the Texans stayed in the playoff hunt with a win over the Chargers. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) INGLEWOOD, Calif. - When C.J. Stroud woke up in his hotel bed Sunday morning in downtown Los Angeles, he was still feeling under the weather. All week he had been dealing with some kind of illness that he said gave him chills and "all the things." He said he barely practiced Thursday. Whatever he had, it was still with him. Yet, some six hours later, he went on to have one of the best games of his career. Stroud, who was playing in front of friends and family near his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga , threw for a season-high 384 yards, a career-high five touchdowns and just one interception in Houston's 44-22 rout of the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The 44 points scored were a season high for the Texans' offense, which has often delivered time and time again, especially on the road. The Texans improved to 3-5 on the season. It was the type of performance that will put Stroud in the MVP conversation if he can continue playing this way. It is the type of performance that will have some suggesting that the Texans can make a run towards the playoffs. "He really gives that confidence to the entire team," coach DeMeco Ryans said of Stroud. "When the defensive guys, they see him up making plays, everyone is excited. Everyone knows the type of energy, the type of momentum that that brings to our entire team when he's making those plays and he's done it all year." The Texans are currently 1 ½ games behind the Patriots for that final wild-card spot with nine games remaining. They face the Browns, who are also 1 ½ games ahead of them, next Sunday in Cleveland. But based on their upcoming schedule, and how Stroud is playing, anything is possible, especially if the defense can gain some momentum too. Though the performance from the defense wasn't perfect, Sunday's game against the NFL's worst offense was a step in the right direction. The Texans tied a franchise record with eight sacks on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. They also forced two turnovers - an interception by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and a fumble. But the offense, which had 485 yards of total offense, was the story of this game. And it started with Stroud, who became just the fourth quarterback younger than 26 years old with at least 350 passing yards and five touchdown passes in multiple games, joining Patrick Mahomes, Dan Marino and Matthew Stafford. The other game Stroud achieved that stat line was during his 2023 rookie season, when he threw five touchdowns in a thrilling 39-37 win over the Bucs . item.title: 3 Former Top Prospects The Pirates Should Sign For Depth
item.description: Jun 2, 2024; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves outfielder Jarred Kelenic (24) runs to first base after hitting a ground ball against the Oakland Athletics during the eighth inning at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Godfree-USA T… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Evan Mazza, Site Editor Good MLB teams have good depth. Having someone interesting at Triple-A that a team can call up in a pinch is always a must. The Pittsburgh Pirates always need depth stashed at Triple-A, and what better way than to give a former top prospect a chance as a change-of-scenery candidate ? With dozens of players recently hitting minor league free agency , the Pirates should take a zero-risk chance on a former top prospect on a minor league contract. At worst, the Pirates sign a player who serves solely as Triple-A depth; at best, they find a diamond in the rough and unlock something the former prospect’s previous team couldn’t. Heston Kjerstad Would Be a Great Fit for the Pirates Heston Kjerstad entered the 2020 draft as one of the best players available and was selected second overall by the Baltimore Orioles. By 2024, he was a consensus top 50 prospect and was looking to make an impact in MLB. Things got off to a promising start for Kjerstad, as he hit for a 113 wRC+ over his first 147 MLB plate appearances in 2023 and 2024. Apr 30, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Orioles outfielder Heston Kjerstad (13) hits a single during the eighth inning against the New York Yankees at Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Mandatory Credit: Reggie Hildred-Imagn Images However, Kjerstad failed to capture a regular role in 2025. In 167 plate appearances, the outfielder hit just .192/.240/.328 with a .248 wOBA and 57 wRC+. He only hit four home runs while striking out over a quarter of the time (26.9%). However, the most worrying part of his first chance at regular playing time was his 3.6% walk rate. Kjerstad spent most of 2026 in the minor leagues, appearing in just 11 MLB games, and struggled to a 28 wRC+ over the small sample size. The O’s released Kjerstad at the end of the season. Although Kjerstad has struggled in his brief MLB time, he has done nothing but hit Triple-A pitching. In 1040 plate appearances dating back to his first look at Triple-A in 2023, the former second overall pick is batting .279/.351/.482 with a .365 wOBA and 115 wRC+. He has walked in 8.6% of his plate appearances, with a 23.9% K%. Kjerstad has plenty of raw power, as indicated by his 89.6 MPH exit velocity; however, his 27% whiff rate is a tad high. Kjerstad, who is primarily an outfielder, also has nearly 400 professional innings at first base. The former top prospect could provide the Pirates with depth at multiple positions. item.title: Michigan Football needs to start planning for a future without Kyle Whittingham
item.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham looks up at the scoreboard during second half action at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Michigan State won the game 15-6. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Over the offseason, excitement built steadily for the 2026 Michigan football season. There were plenty of reasons for optimism with Kyle Whittingham coming in to take over the program. One of the winningest coaches of the 21st century was finally getting the chance to prove himself in a place that’s well-resourced and always has a stream of talent. Instead, the fan base had the wool pulled over its eyes, Michigan’s administration got duped, and the program sits in as bad a place as it’s been since the turn of the century. The idea of hiring Whittingham made a lot of sense last December. Rocked by scandals over the last few years, Michigan needed someone who could stabilize things and be an “adult in the room” while also bringing in enough football acumen to help turn a talented roster into a winner in short order. The “short order” part is key due to Whittingham’s age. At 66, it was clear he’d be in Ann Arbor for only a few years before finally retiring, giving it one last shot to go for a national title. With as much talent as Michigan already had on its roster and the nine wins it had in 2025, no ramp-up was needed. But instead, the team has taken several steps back and looks nowhere close to where it was even at this time last year. This has been most evident over Michigan’s last two games: a sleepy seven-point win at Rutgers, and Saturday’s debacle in which the Wolverines looked totally uninspired and unprepared against a 3-6 Michigan State team. There are three games left, but it’s apparent Michigan has mailed it in, with three more losses surely coming. item.description: The November 9 MetroCard Swipe with takeaways from the America East-Metro Challenge. | Photo by Fairfield Athletics / Design by Hannah Butler (Mid-Major Madness) This story was going to be a continuation of last week’s story with how poorly Thursday went for the Metro. The conference went 3-6 in the home games of the America East-Metro Challenge, setting itself up for a tough mountain to climb on Sunday. But to the league’s credit, they climbed that mountain. The Metro won a bunch of close games to go 5-3 on Sunday, setting up a chance to tie the Challenge should Iona defeat UMBC a week from Monday. Instead of straight doom, here are five takeaways from the Metro-America East Challenge. Dywane Chess is Marist’s most important player John Dunne went out of his way to say that he’s extremely high on freshman Dywane Chess during our preseason interview. He’s looked the part of a Metro Rookie of the Year candidate thanks to his scoring through three games. He dropped 20 points in both of Marist’s America East-Metro Challenge games, leading the Red Foxes in scoring both times. His usage rate through three games is 27.5%, the highest on the team, and he’s played 75% of the team’s minutes as well. Jack Graham and Edward Onyia have taken lower-usage roles than I expected, and Myles Parker still isn’t putting the ball on the floor a ton, so the offensive burden will fall on Chess throughout the year. There will be some games where Brady MacAdams gives Marist a lift – like on Thursday night when he made three triples and scored 17 points – but Chess will have to be the night-in, night-out guy. Chess has a strong frame at 6-foot-4 and has the green light to create off the dribble. He’s already assuming the role of creating mid-range jump shots and getting plenty of spot-up opportunities. I wonder if more pick-and-roll reps are coming as he starts to adapt into a hybrid between the Justin Menard and Elijah Lewis roles. But this all begs the question: will Graham, Onyia, and Parker come along? Graham was solid in the Challenge, but presumably has more in him. Onyia was held scoreless and limited to just 12 minutes in each of the Challenge games. Can those guys give Chess a little more support than they have so far? item.title: Jim Harbaugh is a clown and the Chargers are his circus
item.description: There were 13 minutes remaining in the third quarter when it became clear that Jim Harbaugh checked out. Houston was up 24-9, Tre Harris had just been hurt, adding another injury on offense the Chargers couldn’t endure. Harbz marched along the sideline pre-snap, not watching the next run play, looking like a man who just wanted to keep walking, out of the tunnel, and out of Los Angeles altogether. Perhaps he should. The woes the Chargers have faced this season aren’t entirely of Harbaugh’s creation, but his staggering inability to make changes, or accept what’s best for the team’s future — those are on his shoulders. Harbaugh made headlines prior to Sunday for infamously, nonsensically remaining insistent that the Chargers won’t be trading players away at the deadline because it sends “the message of giving up on the season.” News flash: The Chargers are 0-8 right now. They are dead last in the AFC West, the AFC as a conference, and the NFL as a whole. They are the worst team in football by a country mile, and while Harbz might not like the message they’re “giving up on the season,” they need to give up on the season, because at this point the Chargers are facing another rebuild. It’s impossible to calculate everything wrong for the this season. Injuries wrecked the offensive line, and that started some dominoes falling. The defense is doing its best despite being an afterthought, and while they’re not good by any stretch of the imagination, I hesitate to lump them in with the team’s issues as a whole — because at least they’re performing the basic elements of the job. Offensively, this team has become a dumpster fire. I don’t know the last time a player fell off the map the way that Justin Herbert has this season. item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves made it four wins in a row after beating the Utah Jazz 115-100. LaMelo Ball stole the show as he always does, while Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points. But the bench more than played its part, especially Bones Hyland and Joan Beringer. The former has a nickname for the Frenchman now. Bones Hyland says Joan Beringer is called ‘The Batman’ and shares a ‘funny story’ Beringer suffered a nasal fracture during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ win over the New Orleans Pelicans in the NBA Cup. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re kicking off our 2026 MVBrewers rankings, and the voting for this year’s No. 1 player was perhaps the closest we’ve ever seen: With 74 total votes in our poll on The Feed, catcher William Contreras edged second baseman Brice Turang with 37.9% of the vote (28 votes) compared to 35.1% (26 votes). Jacob Misiorowski garnered 18.9% (14 votes), while Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, and write-in candidate Aaron Ashby each picked up two votes (shoutout to @Berhaltersburner for the recognition). While Turang is a top-three MVP finisher in the league (likely behind Pete Crow-Armstrong and Shohei Ohtani), that’s a regular-season-only award, whereas we don’t have those restrictions here, and perhaps that’s exactly what separates Contreras from Turang. While Contreras ranked seventh on the team in bWAR (2.9) and sixth in fWAR (3.0), he added more immeasurable value than any other player, managing one of baseball’s pitching staffs. He also was an incredible ABS-challenger in the postseason — after an MLB-leading 195 challenges in the regular season at a 56.9% overturn rate, Contreras went 22/33 as a catcher in the postseason, including an incredible 10/13 in the World Series. Contreras also raked all postseason, slashing .373/.448/.588 with three homers, two doubles, nine RBIs, seven runs scored, and a steal across 13 games. And while Contreras had a great postseason, he had nothing to be ashamed of in the regular season. Yes, he turned in just 2.9 bWAR after eclipsing 3.7 WAR in each of his first three seasons with Milwaukee, but he still hit .270/.341/.417 with 18 homers, 27 doubles, 94 RBIs, and 82 runs. Part of the reason his WAR is deflated is a rough stretch from early July to mid-August — across 31 games, he went just 16-for-113, slashing .142/.240/.257 with two homers (one of which was a walk-off homer against the Marlins), five doubles, eight RBIs, and 10 runs scored. item.description: Drake Maye was announced as AFC Offensive Player of October last Wednesday, an honor reflective of his impressive turnaround. After struggling mightily over the first three weeks of the season, the New England Patriots quarterback rebounded nicely to take home the accolade. Four days later, the very same early-season Drake Maye made his return. He helped set the stage for the Patriots getting blown out at the hands of the Green Bay Packers. Maye turned the ball over three times during the 45-27 defeat , tossing a trio of interceptions in the first half that contributed to his team finding itself in an early hole it failed to get out of. And while the second-year passer did have some promising moments as well, those were once again overshadowed by his ball-security concerns. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s starting with me,” Maye said during his post-game presser at Gillette Stadium. “It’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games. I put our defense in a bad spot on the first drive, just gave them the football, had some other chances down the field, and have to see in front.” Sunday’s loss to the Packers was Maye’s second three-interception game of the season, making him the only player in the league with multiple such games on his record. On the year, Maye has now thrown 11 picks — tied with the Chargers’ Justin Herbert for most in the NFL. The first of his picks versus Green Bay already set the tone for the rest of the day. On his first pass attempt, Maye maneuvered a muddy pocket and lifted a floater across the body intended for wide receiver Mack Hollins. Instead of hitting his target, however, the ball landed in the waiting arms of safety Xavier McKinney. McKinney returned the interception 36 yards to set his offense up at the New England 9. Two players later the Packers took a 7-0 lead that continued to grow with the offense unable to find its rhythm. Even when it did, Maye’s interceptions quickly halted any progress. He threw a second pick early in the second period, on a play reminiscent of his first interception of the year. Just like in Week 1, when he was targeting Romeo Doubs deep down the left sideline, he attempted to connect with Kyle Williams only to see the pass broken up and intercepted on the deflection. Two possessions later, after the Patriots had decreased their deficit to 17-7 with a 30-yard touchdown pass from Maye to Rhamondre Stevenson, McKinney registered another pick when he undercut a throw intended for Eli Raridon. “Just throwing the football in spots that I don’t think I should have thrown it,” said Maye about his three INTs. “The first one, I think I just got to see the guys deep, see the safety positions. item.title: Nick Wright calls Patrick Mahomes a ‘cyborg’ after getting injured with hit during Chiefs win over Jets
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes pushed through a serious hit in their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes did not miss a single offensive snap in the win, going 23/31 on pass attempts for 242 yards, two TDs, and a 117.9 passer rating. He also rushed for eight yards on two carries in a strong performance. Mahomes was tackled by Jets EDGE David Bailey in the second quarter and appeared to suffer an elbow injury, but his resolute toughness made him push through the discomfort and finish the win after avoiding major injury. Patrick Mahomes hailed as a cyborg by Nick Wright Watching Mahomes take that rough hit and escape without injury left FOX Sports’ Nick Wright in awe of the 33-year-old QB. “Also… Never a doubt. Mahomes is a cyborg. 99% of QBs have their elbow dislocated on that hit. He missed zero snaps. They’ll be 8-2 heading into Buffalo.” It’s since been confirmed that Mahomes’ injury is an elbow strain/sprain after post-game MRIs, with the QB likely not missing their game against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Mahomes admitted after the win that the hit from Bailey had a major impact on his performance, as he struggled to throw the ball as deep and precisely as he normally can. Nonetheless, even a slightly wounded Mahomes would be a better option than backup QB Justin Fields for the Chiefs right now, especially as they look to challenge the 7-2 Denver Broncos for THE top spot in the AFC West. While Mahomes has not been among the MVP contenders this season, he has had a strong comeback season after rushing through recovery from a torn ACL. Over the season, Mahomes has thrown 177/263 for 2,037 yards, 14 TDs, and four INTs for a 101.8 passer rating. Avoiding a season-ending elbow injury on that play was a moment of good fortune for the Chiefs, and the franchise will hope that fortune pushes them through till the end of the season. item.title: Three-time Olympic judo champion announces bid for French presidency
item.description: Three-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner is to run for the French presidency, with his campaign intending to “show that we can turn France around”. The 37-year-old said he would not run on a left- or right-wing ticket but instead focus his campaign on “bringing the French people together”, with the slogan for his campaign “The France we want”. He told French outlet Le Parisien on Monday: “France is a great country. It has allowed me to become the person I am today and has given me the opportunity to dream big. “Today, that’s what’s missing. That ambition is gone; that hope is gone. “I see a divide in society across the country, but I do not accept what I hear in the mouths of young people, that it is difficult today to imagine a future. That is why I decided to commit myself, alongside the French people, and to become a candidate for the presidency.” An election to decide Emmanuel Macron’s successor is to be held in April next year; Macron, having served two consecutive terms, is ineligible to run again. Riner has no experience of politics but is a well-known and popular figure in France, and has previously hinted at a desire to enter politics at the highest level. He said in an interview last year: “I am a citizen above all, not just a sportsperson. If tomorrow I enter politics, it wouldn’t be to be a minister, it would be to change things. The best role would be president.” Riner, who was born in Guadeloupe, grew up in Paris. He is a nine-time heavyweight world champion, two-time openweight world champion, and has two Olympic bronze medals to go with his three individual golds and two mixed team gold medals. He was a torchbearer during the Olympic torch relay ahead of the 2024 Games in Paris, and lit the cauldron during the opening ceremony alongside retired sprinter Marie-Jose Perec. Riner said that the experience of the home Olympic Games uniting the country inspired him to enter politics, saying: “I saw a whole country come together, proud, happy. I thought to myself, what we have been able to do for 15 days, we must be able to do for the country.” He said his decision to run for president would not end his judo career or hopes of competing at the LA Games 2028.

item.title: MMQB – Turtling Up
item.description: Tell me if you’ve heard this one before during this season: Penn State races out to a big first half lead against an opponent that appears to be hapless, the coaches go into ultra conservative run-out-the-clock mode way too early in the game, and the previously hapless opponent comes roaring back. In the case of the earlier game against Wisconsin, the Lions built a 17-0 first half lead before going conservative, which ultimately bit the team in the ass as the Badgers compiled enough big plays down the stretch to beat the Lions 24-20. In the case of this weekend’s game against Washington, Penn State built a 28-6 halftime lead before going conservative, and the team did just enough to eke out a 28-25 win. Someone needs to have a word with Matt Campbell about not turtling up when he has a lead. Admittedly he is known as a conservative coach, but that’s twice in the same season that he went conservative in the first half of a conference game expecting to just run the clock out for 30+ minutes. I’m not sure what would work in the Big 12, but it sure as hell doesn’t work in the Big Ten. There are play calls that exist that both run the clock but also keep your offense – which was HUMMING in the first half – on the move. It’s not at all necessary to attempt to “kneel out the clock” for two full quarters of the game in all but name via three straight runs up the gut followed by a punt. Some of it is execution, to be fair. This Penn State team seems to have some sort of mental stigma about playing with a lead. They almost don’t believe that they can keep the good juju going, and are all collectively waiting for something to go bad. To hell with that. You’re good enough, obviously, as you built this lead by playing your game in the first half. Keep it up and you dogwalk your opponent. While execution is certainly something to keep an eye on, even that comes from the coaching. This staff needs to trust in themselves and their players and just keep playing like they did to get things going. Who knows if this issue will pop up again this season. Even if it did, at this point I don’t know that Campbell and Co. would do anything different than they’ve been doing. But Matt Campbell is going to need to have a long look in the mirror about just exactly how he expects his Penn State teams going forward to compete in this conference with that sort of mentality. Show some toughness, show some grit, show some belief in your players and coaches, and just go out and play your game. But hey. A win is a win, right?

Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs picked up a dominant 35-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday, but they had a scary moment along the way as superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a big hit to his throwing arm in the second quarter. For a moment, it looked like he could be seriously hurt. Mahomes was able to stay in the game, and an MRI reportedly didn’t reveal any major injury. But after the game, the Chiefs star admitted that the moment scared him, especially after the knee injury that ended his season last year. Mahomes’ Injury Scare Late in the second quarter, Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes’ right arm as he was throwing, with Will McDonald IV and Darrell Jackson Jr. also getting a piece of him on the play. Mahomes grimaced on the ground and then walked off slowly with his arm hanging at his side. But Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw a few warm-up passes, and returned without missing a snap. Chiefs assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer worked on his arm at halftime, and head coach Andy Reid adjusted the game plan in the second half to lean on short throws. Mahomes finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came before the hit. The Chiefs will monitor it for pain and swelling ahead of next Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. ‘That stuff scares you’ Mahomes said after the game that he was always going to try to get back out there despite the injury. “If I’m able to play, I’m going to play,” Mahomes said, via ESPN’s Nate Taylor . “That’s part of the game.
